newsitem.title: USA: Enron, PGE talks with Ore. to resume Mar 6.
newsitem.headline: Enron, PGE talks with Ore. to resume Mar 6.

text.p: Settlement discussions between the Oregon Public Utility Commission (OPUC) staff, Enron Corp and Portland General Electric Co ended Tuesday with no final agreement, but will resume in March.
The OPUC said in a statement late Tuesday all sides agreed to reconvene the discussion on March 6.
"Some progress was made toward resolving customer benefit issues (rate reduction), but much more needs to be done," said Phil Nyegaard, OPUC financial analysis administrator.
Commission staff said they were in conceptual agreement with all but one of the 24 proposed conditions from Enron.

The staff's proposed $189.6 million rate decrease over four years initially was not acceptable to Portland General and Enron, who had proposed a $12 million rate cut from cost savings related to their planned merger.
